Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes

summary: POC scoping call to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a claims-triage/model-infused workflow. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), workload sizing (~5M tokens/day converging on bursty inference), benchmark plan, timeline (2-week baseline POC + 6 week pilot), and decision drivers (security/compliance, latency, cost predictability). Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, compliance deliverables.
topics: Success criteria: latency/p95, accuracy/regression tolerance, cost per 1M tokens
Workload sizing: qps, average sequence length, concurrency, peak vs steady
Benchmarks: baseline hosted run, dedicated pool perf, private on-prem feasibility
Timelines: 2-week POC, 6-8 week pilot, production rollout timing
Decision criteria: security (SOC2/KMS), SLA/uptime, data residency, cost predictability
transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros — I'm Avery from Redwood, our SE Samira and Jordan on CS.
[00:08] Raj: Hi, Raj here, head of ML at Lumen. Maya and Oliver from infra and security with me.
[00:15] Samira: Thanks Raj. The goal today is to scope the POC and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes the most sense for your claims triage workload. We'll cover success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, and timeline.
[00:34] Maya: To be clear, we have strict PII handling and need audit logs retained for 1 year, and a KMS integration if possible.
[00:45] Oliver: Also interested in whether we can keep data inside our VPC or if we need an on-prem option.
[00:52] Avery: Absolutely. quick heads-up, some of our docs call it "Redwood Dedicatede" in older notes, so you might see slightly different names.
[01:10] Raj: For success criteria, our product team wants p95 latency under 300ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens, and end-to-end accuracy not to degrade more than 1.5% compared to our baseline model. Cost target is roughly $X per 1M tokens — we can share a target range.
[01:38] Samira: Got it, p95 < 300ms target. For throughput, can you confirm qps and burst patterns?
[01:46] Raj: Baseline steady is ~15 qps, peaks up to ~120 qps during business hours. Avg seq length ~220 tokens, worst-case 1024 for some investigational prompts. Monthly token volume estimated 5M-15M tokens depending on pilot scope.
[02:08] Maya: We also need SSO (SAML), RBAC per team, and audit trails forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:18] Jordan: Noted. On the deployment side, here's our high-level tradeoff: Hosted = fastest to start, less ops, variable cost; Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for steady throughput and predictable latency, better for isolation; Private = VPC or on-prem gives fullest control for compliance but longer lead time and higher ops.
[02:45] Raj: If Hosted can meet p95 and security needs (VPC peering/private link), we'd prefer to avoid a long private deploy. Cost predictability is a big driver though.
[02:58] Samira: For Dedicated we can size a pool to meet 120 qps peaks with room for KV cache and batching. We'll propose two sizing options during the benchmark: one for cost-optimized (quantized models, batch-friendly) and one latency-optimized (larger GPU, more replicas).
[03:18] Oliver: Important - we need KMS that integrates with our HSM and key rotation policies. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:26] Avery: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private flows and in Hosted via customer-managed keys through our private-link options; I'll send the exact security docs.
[03:36] Raj: Benchmarks — we want to run three lanes: hosted baseline (your hosted endpoint), dedicated pool with our sizing, and a private deployment feasibility test on our infra or a small on-prem node. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and token cost.
[03:55] Samira: We'll need sample payloads (400-600 unique templates) and production-like concurrency patterns. Samira: also, note that some internal benchmarks mis-label K-V cache as K V cache so the logs can look odd.
[04:10] Maya: We'll prepare payloads; want to confirm dataset anonymization steps from you?
[04:17] Samira: Yes we'll share a data spec and masking recommendations.
[04:22] Raj: Timeline — can we do a 2-week quick POC to validate latency/cost on hosted, then a 4-6 week dedicated pilot if results look good?
[04:31] Avery: That matches a typical flow. Week 0-2: baseline hosted run + initial metrics. Week 3-8: dedicated pilot with autoscaling rules and more traffic. Private/on-prem discussion parallel but often takes 8-12 weeks for full infra and security sign-off.
[04:47] Nina: Who will own the pilot infra ops for Dedicated — your team or ours?
[04:54] Jordan: For Dedicated, Redwood manages the serving runtime and capacity, customer provides network peering and credentials. We can offer runbook and optional managed ops add-on.
[05:05] Raj: On costs — please show both per-token hosted and committed reserved pricing for Dedicated. We're sensitive to unit economics.
[05:13] Avery: We'll provide both. We'll also show quantization tradeoffs — 8-bit vs 4-bit. We should be explicit about accuracy delta.
[05:23] Maya: One more security item: we need ephemeral access tokens to rotate and short TTLs for service accounts.
[05:29] Oliver: And audit logs to our S3/GCS bucket or forwarded to Splunk/Datadog.
[05:34] Samira: Both supported; we'll include forwarding options in the security pack.
[05:38] Raj: In terms of decision criteria, to summarize: 1) If Hosted meets p95 and security with private-link, it's preferred for speed of deployment; 2) If cost or predictability requires it, Dedicated is preferred; 3) If regulatory or data residency blocks remote hosting, Private on-prem is necessary.
[06:00] Avery: Exactly. For the POC we'll propose acceptance tests: a) p95 latency < 300ms at 15 qps and within 20% of baseline at 120 qps peak, b) accuracy delta <1.5% on pre-defined eval set, c) audit log presence and KMS integration validated.
[06:20] Raj: Sounds good. Any other gotchas we should know?
[06:25] Samira: Sometimes customers see tokenization differences between model variants — we'll include tokenization alignment steps. Also, for very long contexts the KV cache behavior matters; we'll test cache warmup in the benchmark.
[06:40] Maya: For the Dedicated sizing, can you propose both GPU types? We have preference for A100-type equivalence but cost might push us toward T4-like or L4-equivalent.
[06:52] Samira: Yep, we'll provide two sizing recommendations with expected qps/latency and cost numbers. We'll also show how batching windows affect p95 vs avg cost.
[07:05] Raj: On legal/procurement, we'd like an outline of contract terms for Dedicated (commit sizes, overage rules) so procurement can review ahead of pilot.
[07:15] Avery: We'll include a sample SOW and the commitment models in the pricing doc.
[07:22] Nina: Can you share references for insurance customers who did similar pilots?
[07:27] Avery: We have a couple redacted references; I'll include a short case study.
[07:33] Raj: Great. Operationally, who will be the single point of contact?
[07:36] Jordan: Jordan will be CSM and primary POC for pilot operations, Avery for commercial, Samira for technical.
[07:42] Maya: Any requirements from our side for the hosted baseline run?
[07:45] Samira: We need sample payloads, traffic pattern CSV, auth test accounts, and a small eval set. We'll share the exact spec in a doc.
[07:56] Oliver: For private/on-prem, rough ETA if we go that route?
[07:59] Avery: Typically 8-12 weeks for on-prem, depends on networking approvals and security review. Some customers do a hybrid — host model runtime in their VPC with Redwood control plane in private mode, that shortens time.
[08:16] Raj: OK let's lock next steps.
[08:19] Avery: Recap: We will send pricing and SOW, Samira sends benchmark plan and data spec, Oliver shares compliance checklist. Schedule baseline run week of 2026-12-12.
[08:31] Nina: thanks everyone, this is helpful.
[08:34] Raj: Thanks.
[49:50] (end)
